verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents a public v2 REST API with Bearer API-key and OAuth authentication and published rate limits. It covers bookings (create, reschedule), slots, event types, schedules and webhooks, and its agent docs explicitly position the API for AI agents to check availability and create bookings. The docs are served as fetchable markdown (probe HTTP 200). Missing for 10: a discoverable machine-readable OpenAPI spec (all probed paths returned 404), independent hands-on corroboration of API usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Cal.com API has 3 authentication methods: 1. OAuth 2. API key 3. Platform (Deprecated)
Authentication to the API is performed via the Authorization header. For example, the request would go something like: 'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'
POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings.
Cal.com API v2 enables AI agents to: Check availability - Query available time slots for any user or team, Create bookings - Schedule meetings on behalf of users
Cal.com offers a v2 REST API, embeddable React components (Cal Atoms), an embed flow, and a hosted MCP server for AI agents.
